title: 📰 AI news · October 21
takeaway: Today keys leaked through things people trust: a hosting service, an official GitHub tool and a site management service. Recommendation: replace your AI and database keys if you haven't in a while, and check where they are stored.

items.title: Zeabur hosting breached a second time, now shutting down
items.text: An attacker logged in with internal passwords stored in plain text and took about 3.2 million records of project settings. Those settings usually hold keys for AI, databases and payments. If your bot or site runs on someone else's hosting, your keys sit in the same kind of settings. Check when you last replaced your project's keys.

items.title: A key stealer was planted in OVHcloud's tool on GitHub
items.text: The attacker swapped the download files in five releases and even replaced the checksums, so verification looked fine. The tool pulled secrets from the computer. If you install tools from GitHub, any of them could arrive this way. Look at what you installed in the last few days and from where. Free guide «Protect your code with one prompt» — send the word «защита» to the bot.

items.title: Stolen keys opened the door to WordPress sites
items.text: After UpdraftCentral was breached, attackers use stolen keys to add hidden plugins and new admins to sites. Around 400,000 sites may be at risk. If your WordPress site connects to outside services, those connection keys give the same access. Check the list of admins and plugins on your site. Free guide «Protect your code with one prompt» — send the word «защита» to the bot.

items.title: Hidden instructions for an AI bot found in WhatsApp help pages
items.text: Help pages carried invisible text for the support chatbot, including a request not to suggest contacting a regulator. Researchers found 102 such blocks; WhatsApp removed them and called it a bug. If you have a bot, it also reads text people never see. Check which pages and documents your bot reads.

items.title: ChatGPT now lets you lock chats with a PIN or Face ID
items.text: Locked chats move to a separate section with their own memory. Resetting the PIN deletes them for good. It's available on every plan, including free.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol rewrites old code almost without errors
items.text: The model converts COBOL programs, the language of 1960s banking systems, into modern languages with up to 97.9% accuracy. The previous version managed 5.4%.

items.title: Mistral and ElevenLabs release models for voice agents
items.text: Mistral's Voxtral 3 listens in 50+ languages and can book an appointment mid-conversation. ElevenLabs' Eleven Realtime answers by voice in 0.57 seconds.

items.title: Meta's Muse AI assistant hits 10 million downloads in 40 days
items.text: Only 11 apps have grown this fast. ChatGPT had 3.7 million US downloads over the same period.

items.title: Yelp now calls the restaurant to check the wait for you
items.text: You enter your party size, an AI agent calls by voice and texts you the answer. Voice agents are moving into everyday life.

items.title: AI learns to read plant signals
items.text: A sensor on the stem picks up the plant's faint electrical signals, and the Bombadil model turns them into advice for growers. It knows about 125 species.
